title_text: Two tricks to trivialize higher-indexed families

Inline.Text: The conventional general syntax of indexed families in dependent type theories follow the style of “constructors returning a special case”, as in Agda, Lean, Idris, Coq, and probably many other systems. Fording is a method to encode indexed families of this style with index-free inductive types and an identity type. There is another trick that merges interleaved higher inductive-inductive types into a single big family of types. It makes use of a small universe as the index to distinguish the original types. In this paper, we show that these two methods can trivialize some very fancy-looking indexed families with higher inductive indices (which we refer to as higher indexed families).
